symptom: The first command after upgrading to the unit-index-2 format (or on a fresh clone) opened every unit file to build the index — 641 opens where the previous build opened 383 — with no explanation, a visible stall on Windows where an open costs about a millisecond.
cause: By design the index is a pure cache and a cold build reads everything; nothing said it was happening. The new format stores Name and Excluded, which the old unit-types.idx never had, so it cannot be seeded from the old file.
insight: A one-time cost a user cannot see reads as a regression; one line on stderr turns it into an expected step. Keep the notice in the library behind a nil-by-default writer (mpr.ColdUnitIndexNotice) that the CLI sets with the banner, so quiet mode and library callers stay silent, and count units before buildUnitCache opens its row query rather than during it.
